tier_reason: First-party docs/benchmark.md states the CPU (Xeon E5-2630 v4 @ 2.20GHz, 40 cores), GCC 4.8.5, NIC and OS, and the workflow server code is public (benchmark/benchmark-01-http_server.cc). Optimization flags are not stated on the page (only implied by the RelWithDebInfo default in benchmark/CMakeLists.txt), and the nginx config and brpc server code are not published, so the baseline side is not reproducible and it is not A; first-party, so not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Read off the docs/benchmark.md charts (derived from page data). QPS vs concurrency (benchmark-01.png): at concurrency 256-2048, workflow ~490-530K QPS vs nginx ~203-213K for 64B/512B bodies (~2.3-2.6x) and ~442-458K vs ~180-205K for 4096B (~2.2-2.5x); the gap is small at concurrency 1-4, where brpc leads. QPS vs body length (benchmark-02.png): workflow ~425-545K vs nginx ~165-220K up to 4KB, but at 8-16KB the workflow-512 and nginx-512 curves nearly meet (~202K vs ~195K; ~166K vs ~163K) and at 32KB/64KB all servers converge at ~88K/~45K. Latency: at fixed body size workflow is lower than nginx as concurrency grows (~4.0-4.5ms vs ~12.4-14.1ms at concurrency 2048), but at concurrency 512 with 16KB/32KB bodies workflow latency (~8ms/~18ms) is higher than nginx (~4ms/~9ms) (benchmark-04.png). The prose states only that workflow 'can maintain 500K QPS' for 64B and 512B bodies at sufficient concurrency and that it beats brpc and nginx throughout the QPS curves.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 4.8.5 stated on the page; optimization flags are not stated. benchmark/CMakeLists.txt (initial 2020 commit) defaults to CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE RelWithDebInfo with -Wall -fPIC -pipe -std=c++11 -fno-exceptions. nginx and brpc build options are not stated.
corrections.hardware: Two identical machines (server and client, ~0.1ms RTT): Intel Xeon E5-2630 v4 @ 2.20GHz, '40 Cores' x86_64 (socket count not stated), 192GB RAM, 25000Mbps NIC, CentOS 7.8.2003, kernel 3.10.0-1127.el7.x86_64
corrections.workload: Minimal HTTP server returning a fixed random ASCII body (with Date/Content-Type headers); concurrency doubled over 1-2048 and body size doubled over 16B-64KB (orthogonal), load from wrk/wrk2 on a separate machine. workflow ran 16 poller + 20 handler threads; nginx 40 worker processes; brpc 40 threads. A second test measured latency CDFs vs brpc only (concurrency 1024, 1KB bodies, 20K/100K/200K QPS with 1% 5ms slow requests).
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark from the 2020 docs (GCC 4.8.5, kernel 3.10). Results are PNG charts; only the ~500K QPS figure is in prose, and the page says only selected concurrency/length combinations are plotted. nginx config and brpc server code are not published, and their tuning (40 workers/threads) was chosen by the workflow authors. The advantage over nginx vanishes at large bodies: QPS converges at 16-64KB (likely bandwidth-bound on the 25Gbps NIC), and at concurrency 512 with 16KB/32KB bodies workflow latency is higher than nginx. brpc is slightly ahead at concurrency 1-4 and at 20K QPS in the latency CDF.

notes: Real entry with a genuine nginx comparison, but tier A was too high (flags unstated on page, baseline configs unpublished) and 'consistently better across all combinations' is overstated: the charts show convergence at 16-64KB bodies and worse latency than nginx at 16/32KB, concurrency 512. Metadata verified: Apache-2.0, not a fork, not archived, 14,424 stars, last commit 2026-08-10 (active).

tier_reason: Well-known independent suite (the-benchmarker/web-frameworks) with public code (c/agoo-c/config.yaml, c/agoo-c/Makefile, c/agoo-c/simple.c, c/Dockerfile, go/nethttp/main.go, .tasks/config.rake) and build flags derivable from it. Not A: the CPU name in data.json is a string hardcoded in .tasks/db.rake, not a measured CPU model, and the GCC version is only implied by the debian:trixie-slim base image.

corrections.claimed_speedup: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks data.json of 2026-09-24 (develop branch, commit f673364): agoo-c 0.7 (release v0.7.3) 74,974 / 141,394 / 149,193 req/s at concurrency 64 / 256 / 512 vs Go net/http ('nethttp', label 1.22) 71,499 / 67,382 / 67,239 req/s, i.e. 1.05x / 2.10x / 2.22x (derived from page data)
corrections.workload: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks run of 2026-09-24: `zrk --plain --closed` (closed loop over keep-alive connections, not oha), 15 s at each concurrency level 64/256/512. Each headline number is the average over the routes in .env (GET /, GET /user/0, POST /user; SQL avg in .tasks/db.rake), all hello-world handlers. The framework container is pinned to cores 0-3 (SERVER_CPUS) and the load generator to cores 4-15.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: debian:trixie-slim + build-essential (Debian trixie default GCC is 14.2; the suite does not print the version). libagoo v0.7.3 is built with a plain `cd agoo-c/src && make`, which without build=release selects the debug flags `-g -Og -std=gnu11` (agoo-c src/Makefile). The benchmark app simple.c is compiled with `-O3 -std=gnu11` (c/agoo-c/Makefile). Go side: golang:1.27 image, `go build -trimpath`, GOAMD64=v3.
corrections.hardware: Single shared host per data.json: 16 CPUs (Etc.nprocessors), Linux 7.2.6-200.fc44.x86_64. The cpu_name 'M1 Eight-Core Processor' and memory 7,733,008 kB are hardcoded in .tasks/db.rake, not measured, so the CPU model is unknown; a comment in go/Dockerfile names an AMD Ryzen 7 5700U, not confirmed for this run. Server container limited to 4 cores (SERVER_CPUS=0-3), load generator on cores 4-15.
corrections.caveats: Single suite run: data.json is overwritten on every run, and the suite says results from different method revisions are not comparable. At concurrency 64 agoo-c's server_cpu_saturation was only 0.58 (2.34 of 4 cores), below the suite's 75% server-bound threshold, so the c=64 figure is not a clean framework number; at 256/512 it was 0.99. Earlier snapshots vary widely. Master data.json of 2026-09-20 (older zrk method, no core pinning) shows 95,173 / 124,024 / 114,466 vs nethttp 96,149 / 85,406 / 83,964 req/s (0.99x / 1.45x / 1.36x). Under the pre-September oha method (a new connection per request, June-August 2026) agoo-c recorded only ~1.3-2.0K req/s vs nethttp ~2.1-26K, so it was slower there. The suite builds libagoo in its default debug mode (-g -Og), which likely understates agoo-c. The tested release v0.7.3 dates from 2019-11-10, and there are no commits since 2020-12-16.

notes: The record's numbers are on the develop-branch (default) data.json, commit f673364, not the master URL it cited; master currently shows only 0.99x-1.45x. benchmark_url is now pinned to that commit, and the load generator is corrected from oha to zrk --closed. The odd c=64 dip is explained by the suite's own saturation probe (server only 58% busy). Metadata verified: MIT, not a fork, not archived, 153 stars, last commit 2020-12-16 (abandoned).

tier_reason: Well-known independent suite (the-benchmarker/web-frameworks) runs CWIST and Go net/http on one host with public code (c/cwist/config.yaml, c/cwist/main.c, c/Dockerfile, go/nethttp/main.go, .tasks/config.rake) and flags visible in the build files. Not A: the CPU name in data.json is a string hardcoded in .tasks/db.rake, not a measured CPU model, and the GCC version is only implied by the debian:trixie-slim base image.

corrections.claimed_speedup: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks data.json of 2026-09-24 (develop branch, commit f673364): CWIST 3.6 148,679 / 154,723 / 151,250 req/s at concurrency 64 / 256 / 512 vs Go net/http ('nethttp', label 1.22) 71,499 / 67,382 / 67,239 req/s, i.e. 2.08x / 2.30x / 2.25x (derived from page data)
corrections.workload: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks run of 2026-09-24: `zrk --plain --closed` (closed loop over keep-alive connections, not oha), 15 s at each concurrency level 64/256/512. Each headline number is the average over the routes in .env (GET /, GET /user/0, POST /user; SQL avg in .tasks/db.rake), all hello-world handlers. The framework container is pinned to cores 0-3 (SERVER_CPUS) and the load generator to cores 4-15; CWIST's server_cpu_saturation was about 0.99 on about 3.95-3.98 cores at every level (server-bound by the suite's own probe).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: debian:trixie-slim + build-essential (Debian trixie default GCC is 14.2; the suite does not print the version). libcwist v3.6 is built with its own Makefile (`make -j$(nproc)`), whose GCC profile is `-Ofast -g -flto=auto -ffat-lto-objects -fno-plt -falign-*=32 -fno-semantic-interposition -fomit-frame-pointer -finline-functions -fstrict-aliasing -funroll-loops`, plus -fstack-protector-strong -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 on Linux. The benchmark main.c is compiled with `gcc -O2` (c/cwist/config.yaml). Go side: golang:1.27 image, `go build -trimpath`, GOAMD64=v3.
corrections.hardware: Single shared host per data.json: 16 CPUs (Etc.nprocessors), Linux 7.2.6-200.fc44.x86_64. The cpu_name 'M1 Eight-Core Processor' and memory 7,733,008 kB are hardcoded in .tasks/db.rake, not measured, so the CPU model is unknown; a comment in go/Dockerfile names an AMD Ryzen 7 5700U, not confirmed for this run. Server container limited to 4 cores (SERVER_CPUS=0-3), load generator on cores 4-15.
corrections.caveats: Single suite run: data.json is overwritten on every run, and the suite says results from different method revisions are not comparable. Earlier snapshots with CWIST 3.4-3.5 under the older zrk method show only a small lead over net/http. Master data.json of 2026-09-20 (CWIST 3.5): 101,254 / 89,553 / 87,455 vs 96,149 / 85,406 / 83,964 req/s (1.04x-1.05x). Snapshot of 2026-09-15 (CWIST 3.5): 142.8K / 120.9K / 119.0K vs 133.1K / 112.2K / 109.9K (~1.07-1.08x). The suite entry (c/cwist/config.yaml, main.c) is maintained by CWIST's lead developer (gg582 authors its version bumps, and the file header says it is mirrored from CWIST's benchmarks/web-frameworks/), so the implementation is first-party-tuned, though the suite runs it. CWIST's own README benchmark has it slightly behind Rust Axum (117,184 vs 121,272 req/s). Very young project with a low star count (15) and no independent track record. It vendors BoringSSL, lsquic, SQLite, cJSON and others under their own licenses.

notes: The record's numbers are on the develop-branch (default) data.json, commit f673364, not the master URL it cited; master (CWIST 3.5, older method) shows only a ~1.05x lead. benchmark_url is now pinned to that commit, and the load generator is corrected from oha to zrk --closed. The 2.1-2.3x lead appears in only one run and one CWIST version (3.6). Metadata verified: MIT, not a fork, not archived, 15 stars, last commit 2026-09-25 (active).
